Our story

akyn \akin\

  1. noun a non-traditional family
  2. adjective something like wine

Made in the former grain silos of a turn of the 20th century southern Virginia grist mill, these wines are anything but ordinary. Formed in 2020 by a group of friends living in the Washington DC area, akyn takes its name from the first letter of each of the last names of its owners. Hybrid grape varietals and low intervention in wine-making processes produce vibrant and unique offerings that pair well with abuela’s chorizo and eggs as with haute cuisine.

After purchasing the lovely property at Watts Mill in Chatham, VA on the eve of the COVID-19 pandemic, we set about trying to figure out if it was possible to make wine there. After some years, numerous helping hands, many HARD-earned lessons and lots of fun, we are feeling pretty good about answering that question with a “yes.”

In general, we make ‘natural wine’ ie. spontaneously fermented wine with the indigenous yeast found in the grape skins and adding nothing to the process except for minimal sulfur if the wine calls for it. No filtering, no fining. We are also working almost exclusively with hybrid grape varietals because the vines that produce them are better suited for the southern Virginia climate and thus don’t require as much spraying or chemical intervention in the vineyard. Since these lesser known grapes don’t have well established styles and expectations, we are free to experiment with them in all kinds of fun ways and also means that unless you, too, are an east coast natty wine nerd, you may not have heard of them.

The wines you’ll find here represent an important step in our journey to figure out how we want to make and present wines as we learn our site, the regional fruit and what’s possible given the realities of our little crew and stage of life.

2025

gary

Chambourcin Traminette
2025 · Virginia

Named after our dearly departed pet guinea hen, Gary is a 50/50 blend of red and white. Berries on the nose, acid on the palate. Give it a chill and enjoy.

50% Chambourcin, 50% Traminette
13% ABV  ·  20 cases produced
Native yeast.

pithy

Skin Contact Traminette
2025 · Virginia

We call this one “pithy” both because the predominant aromatic is perfumed grapefruit peel and because it’s a no-brainer to pair with intensely flavored food. Orange rhymes with everything.

75% Traminette, 25% Chardonel
11.5% ABV  ·  20 cases produced
Native yeast.

chardonel

Chardonel
2025 · Virginia

Chardonel is an apple forward hybrid of Chardonnay that grows very well in Virginia. It’s not your mom’s buttery Chardonnay, but it’s also not, not that.

100% Chardonel
14% ABV  ·  20 cases produced
Native yeast.

2024 & earlier

red white blend

Chambourcin Traminette
2024 · Virginia

Although this wine is nearly 20% white, the intense color of the Chambourcin gives it the appearance of a deeply macerated red wine. But don’t let appearances deceive you. This drinks like a juicy, berry-forward white wine.

83% Chambourcin, 17% Traminette
13% ABV  ·  20 cases produced
Native yeast.

pithy

Skin Contact Traminette
2024 · Virginia

Traminette is a highly aromatic Gewürztraminer hybrid. At barely 11%, it is very easy drinking. Much more high-toned and citrusy than orange wines you may be used to, this wine is extremely light on the palate and stands up to bold flavors.

100% Traminette
11% ABV  ·  20 cases produced
Native yeast.

chardonel

Chardonel
2023 · Virginia

Light skin contact, oxidative but still fruity, more ambition than know-how, happy accidents.

100% Chardonel
13% ABV  ·  25 cases produced
Native yeast.
